profile.summary:
🚀 Innovative Senior Software Engineer | Blockchain Patent Inventor | Passion for AI/ML Infra Development

Hello! I’m a dynamic Senior Software Engineer with a proven track record of driving innovation in the tech industry. I’m proud to have successfully submitted a blockchain patent within just six months of starting my first job, where I was the primary inventor. This accomplishment came from my initiative and close collaboration with my Tech Lead, who provided invaluable guidance and design feedback.

🎮 From Pro-Gamer to Tech Pioneer:
Before diving into the world of software engineering, I was deeply involved in the competitive gaming scene, participating in Gamebattles/MLG circuits for Gears of War 2 and Call of Duty Modern Warfare 2. Though I’ve transitioned from gaming to tech, my passion for driving innovation and thinking outside the box remains stronger than ever.

💡 Professional Highlights:

	•	Collaborated with the Salesforce Patent team on a blockchain application for the finance industry, addressing scalability challenges and optimizing financial transactions for SEC audits.
	•	Proficient in Java, Python, Golang, and TypeScript, with a solid foundation in AI/ML and full-stack development. My approach involves a keen focus on customer needs, data-driven decision-making, and roadmap contributions.
	•	Earned a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science from Georgia Institute of Technology with a GPA of 3.9.

🌟 Interests & Passions:

	•	Venture Capitalism and Crypto/Blockchain: Authored a patent-pending blockchain project in my first year post-college.
	•	Enthusiastic about Computer Architecture, Cloud/Distributed Systems, Microservices, and system design strategies.
	•	Active in the Silicon Valley startup scene, an avid reader of tech and startup articles on Medium, and a follower of open-source projects and financial markets on platforms like Reddit and Discord.

🏔️ Personal Interests:
When not immersed in the tech world, I enjoy skiing, cooking, scuba diving, and volunteering, embracing a well-rounded and active lifestyle.

positions.title: Senior Robotics/ML Software Engineer
positions.locationName: San Francisco, California, United States · On-site
positions.description:
At Cruise, I’ve combined deep software engineering expertise with machine learning to advance autonomous vehicle technology. My work has focused on the AV Remote Platform (enabling remote assistance for AVs) and Marketplace Engineering (optimizing ride-hail supply dynamics).

Technical Expertise & ML Integration
	•	Spearheaded the development of critical services using Golang, TypeScript, and Python to integrate ML into infrastructure, enhancing predictive analytics and vehicle routing.
	•	Deployed high-performance HTTP and gRPC applications with real-time capabilities using websockets and WebRTC, supporting ML-driven decision-making in autonomous navigation.
	•	Leveraged machine learning models to refine real-time data processing and decision-making, improving vehicle response accuracy and ride efficiency.

Cloud Infrastructure & ML Deployment
	•	Built and maintained CI/CD pipelines and Docker-based orchestration, streamlining the deployment of ML models from development to production.
	•	Managed complex data infrastructure with Redis, Postgres, and GCP Spanner, ensuring high availability and low-latency access for ML-driven applications.
	•	Led multi-region cloud deployments to enhance the resilience and scalability of ML-based services.

Leadership & Cost Optimization
	•	Directed a team of engineers to internalize key services and cutting costs by $550,000 annually by replacing Twilio & Datadog third-party dependencies with in-house solutions.
	•	Championed cross-functional collaboration to align ML development with engineering goals, accelerating time-to-market for new features.

Technologies & Tools
	•	Languages: Golang, TypeScript, Python
	•	Infrastructure: Kubernetes, Terraform, Docker, GCP
	•	Data: Redis, Postgres, GCP Spanner
	•	Networking: HTTP, gRPC, WebRTC, Websockets

patents.title: Using cache objects to store events for adding corresponding objects in a blockchain
patents.description: Methods and systems are described for using cache objects to store events for adding corresponding objects in a blockchain. In one implementation, a first cache object is identified. The cache object stores events published responsive to updates, insertions, or deletions of records in a database object. An identifier for the cache object is based on a time window with which the cache object is associated, and an identifier for the database object. Events are retrieved from a cache that includes the cache object, based on the identifier for the cache object. The events were stored in the cache object during the time window. A block is added to a blockchain. The block's payload includes objects corresponding to a subset of the events.
